critique.good: Equal month widths keep headers and sales figures intact and make the measures easy to compare. All region names wrap at word boundaries.
critique.problems: The narrow region column makes every label wrap, with Europe, Middle East & Africa occupying four lines. The resulting tall rows weaken the connection between each label and its figures. June and part of May require horizontal scrolling.
critique.cause: The 78px region column leaves 57px for text. Each 59px month column leaves the 38px needed by the widest sales figure, so the intact table exceeds the viewport.

critique.good: The wider region column gives the labels a more comfortable rhythm: two fit on one line, and the longest uses three lines. Equal month columns preserve intact figures and support comparison.
critique.problems: Less of the monthly series is visible initially: May and June require scrolling, with May starting beyond the viewport. North America still wraps, while the long label remains taller than the other rows.
critique.cause: The 120px region column leaves 99px for text but takes 42px more viewport space than r0A. Six 59px month columns bring the total to 475px.

critique.good: All six months are visible within the viewport, and the month columns have a consistent rhythm.
critique.problems: Region names, two headers, and many sales figures split across lines, including within numbers. The unusually tall rows and fragmented values make both across-row and down-column comparison difficult.
critique.cause: The 65px region column leaves only 44px for text, less than the longest individual word. Each 49px month column leaves 28px, less than the 38px needed for the widest figures and some headers.

critique.good: The six equal monthly columns create a consistent comparison rhythm, and the figures and month headings remain intact. More of the monthly sequence is visible initially than in the other designs.
critique.problems: Every region name wraps, and the long Europe label occupies four lines. The resulting tall rows make comparisons down a month less compact.
critique.cause: The 95px region column leaves 74px for text. The 59px monthly columns are wide enough to preserve their contents but put the last 90px of the table beyond the viewport.

critique.good: The wider region column reduces the longest label to three lines and keeps Asia Pacific on one line. Equal monthly widths preserve the parallel structure and intact figures.
critique.problems: North America and Latin America still wrap, while the viewport cuts into May. Readers must scroll to see the end of the monthly sequence.
critique.cause: The 110px region column leaves 89px for text, improving the labels but increasing overflow to 105px. Each month still needs 59px to keep its longest figure intact.

critique.good: All labels and values fit on one line, producing compact rows and easy comparisons within the visible columns.
critique.problems: The region column takes up much of the initial view, leaving only two complete months visible. Following a region across all six months requires substantial horizontal scrolling.
critique.cause: The 216px region column accommodates the longest label on one line but pushes the 571px table 211px beyond the viewport.

critique.good: The region labels are easy to scan, with only the long Europe, Middle East & Africa label wrapping. Equal month widths keep the figures aligned and intact.
critique.problems: The reader must scroll to see the later months, which makes comparing all six months across a row less immediate.
critique.cause: The 125px region column and six 59px month columns produce a 480px table, 120px wider than the viewport.

critique.good: All words and sales figures remain intact, and more months are visible initially than in the other designs. The equal month widths support comparison.
critique.problems: Most region names wrap, and the four-line Europe label makes its row much taller than the others. The resulting vertical spread makes the table harder to scan as a whole.
critique.cause: The 80px region column leaves only 59px for text. The six 59px month columns still make the table 75px wider than the viewport.

critique.good: Region labels are easy to read, sales figures stay intact, and the month columns have a consistent rhythm.
critique.problems: The wider region column does not reduce the table height or the longest label's line count compared with r2A, but it pushes more monthly data beyond the viewport.
critique.cause: The 150px region column adds 25px to r2A without changing its row heights; the table overflows by 145px.

r0A.idea: Keep every word and sales figure intact with a compact region column, accepting horizontal scrolling to reach later months.

r0B.idea: Give region names more room and use fewer lines for labels, at the cost of more horizontal scrolling.

r0C.idea: Fit all seven columns within 359px, accepting splits in longer region words and sales figures to show every month at once.

r1A.idea: Widen the region column from r0A while retaining the minimum equal widths that keep monthly figures intact. Test whether the labels gain a better rhythm for a modest increase in scrolling.

r1B.idea: Try a region width between r0A and r0B, seeking shorter labels and rows while recovering some initial visibility of May.

r1C.idea: Give the longest region label its full one-line width to test a compact, consistently single-line row layout. This makes substantially fewer months visible initially and requires more horizontal scrolling.

r2A.idea: Give region names a little more room than in r1B while keeping the months equal and intact. This tests whether more labels can stay on one line without the large scrolling cost of r1C.

r2B.idea: Use the minimum width that preserves the longest individual region word. This tests a narrower, more scroll-efficient layout while accepting taller wrapped labels.

r2C.idea: Explore an intermediate region width that may shorten the longest label further, while retaining substantially less overflow than the all-one-line design.

r3A.idea: Reduce the region column from r2A to gain 15px of initial monthly visibility while testing whether the labels retain a compact wrapping pattern.

r3B.idea: Try a middle ground between r2A and r2B: give the region labels more room than r2B while reducing horizontal scrolling by 25px from r2A.

r3C.idea: Test the narrowest region column supported by the stated longest word, leaving 57px for text. This explores the maximum initial visibility possible while keeping words and figures intact.

understanding.purpose: Compare regional sales across the first six months of the year.
understanding.reading: Readers scan across a region to follow its monthly sales and down each month to compare regions.
groups: Jan through Jun are parallel monthly measures and benefit from equal widths.
Region labels identify the rows and need enough space to remain easy to associate with their values.
may_wrap: Region names can wrap at spaces; the longer Europe, Middle East & Africa label will need several lines in a narrow column.

bad.why: The narrow region column wraps every label and stretches the longest to four lines, weakening row scanning for a modest reduction in scrolling.
The longest region occupies four lines and two other labels wrap, producing uneven row heights without bringing another complete month into view.
The narrow region column wraps every label and stretches the longest to four lines, making the table tall and harder to scan.

final.rationale: r2A keeps three region labels on one line and the longest to two, giving the rows a compact, readable rhythm. The six equal month columns preserve intact values and make comparisons easy. Four complete months are visible initially, with the remaining two reached by scrolling.

general: Give row identifiers enough width to remain easy to recognize and follow across the table.
Columns with the same role benefit from consistent widths when their contents have similar needs.
Judge the amount of scrolling alongside the readability gained by wider columns.
specific: All six month columns need approximately the same width for their values.
A 125px region column keeps all but the longest label on one line; giving it substantially more width adds scrolling without reducing the longest label below two lines in r2C.

final.tradeoffs: r1C keeps every row on one line but shows fewer months initially and requires substantially more scrolling. Narrower region columns bring more of the later months into view but create taller, less even rows.
final.uncertain: A designer prioritizing single-line labels may prefer r1C, while one prioritizing a wider initial view of the months may accept r1B or r3A. The ranges are approximate and assume the month columns remain equal.

A.why: The table fits the viewport, but region names and several sales figures split across lines, making both row identification and comparisons difficult.

B.why: Region names and figures stay intact, but the wide region column leaves only two full months visible initially, making comparison across months costly.

C.why: Names wrap at word boundaries and figures remain intact. Four months are fully visible, with May partly visible and the remaining columns reached by scrolling.

D.why: The region column keeps most names on one line and the long name on two. Four complete months fit initially, with intact figures and compact, easy-to-scan rows.

E.why: Names wrap without breaking words, and the figures stay intact. Four complete months fit initially, though the narrow region column makes several rows taller.

F.why: The region names wrap cleanly and the figures remain intact. Four complete months fit initially, though several row labels take more lines than in D.

reviews.unsure: The screenshots show only part of the horizontally overflowing tables, so the assessment of their remaining columns relies on the stated content facts and the visible column rhythm.

A.why: Region names and values stay intact, but the wide region column leaves only two complete months visible initially, making comparison across months dependent on scrolling.

B.why: The table fits the viewport, but region names and many four-digit values split inside words and numbers. Tall rows make comparisons difficult.

C.why: Four complete months fit initially, values stay intact, and region names wrap at word boundaries. The longer region label takes three lines, and later months require scrolling.

D.why: Values stay intact and almost five months are visible, but the narrow region column makes several labels wrap and stretches the longest label over four lines.

E.why: Four complete months fit initially, values stay intact, and the wider region column keeps most labels on one line. The longest label wraps cleanly into two lines, preserving compact, readable rows.

F.why: Values stay intact and almost five months are visible. The narrow region column makes several labels wrap, with the longest spanning four lines and creating a tall row.

reviews.unsure: D and F appear very similar; their small differences are difficult to judge from the screenshots. The preference for E depends on valuing easier row-label scanning over seeing more of May initially.
